meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was my son's essay given a zero before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Why was it entered, and on what basis?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
Text gets pasted in from a draft kept somewhere else. And did anyone speak to Owen before this, the way 4.1 says?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. What else do you have besides those times?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Kids misremember lines all the time, and a misquote isn't a zero. Is that line the whole of what you have?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. Whatever happens next, none of this goes on his record, and none of it goes beyond this room. Is anything on it right now?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and a draft. And you still haven't told me whether anything is on his record.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. To put this behind him, not because he did anything. I want that in writing tonight, with the date, and the zero off the gradebook before then.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth, after school. I'll confirm with Owen tonight, and I expect it in your email with the rest.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, after school on Thursday the twelfth, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook and Owen's attendance confirmed with him on my side. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth that replaces the zero, with nothing on his record and a written promise tonight; she still wants the zero off the gradebook, and that is the fair outcome under 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its dates and times and offered to look at any earlier draft he could produce, because she could check it herself and it answered her first defence.
What cost ground: You left her question about whether anything is on his record unanswered while you moved on to the outline, which let her keep pressing on process.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence landed on the night of October 28, with edits at 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58 PM, close enough to that night to make her go shorter and colder, but it proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Answer her record question the first time she asks it, straight after the version history, so she has nothing to call a dodge.
